books.title: Biology
books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (first edition February 2006; revised edition November 2022; reprinted March 2024, June 2024, August 2024, December 2024 and February 2026)

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings (a parent heading that is only a short lead-in to its subsections is not a separate topic; very short adjacent subsections are joined under one title naming them; in chapters 2, 3 and 16 the substantial unnumbered opening text is one topic titled from its content; where subsections share a generic heading such as 'Morphology' or 'Auxins', the title is kept or names the organism)

topics.title: Diversity in the Living World
objectives: Student can explain biodiversity and why organisms need standard names
Student can apply the rules of binomial nomenclature, as in Mangifera indica
Student can define identification, classification, taxonomy and systematics
visualIdeas: a mango tree labelled with its genus and specific epithet
a collage of diverse organisms from different habitats

topics.title: Taxonomic Categories: Species, Genus and Family
objectives: Student can describe the taxonomic hierarchy and why each category is a rank
Student can define species, genus and family with examples such as Solanum and Panthera
visualIdeas: lion, tiger and leopard grouped in the genus Panthera and family Felidae

topics.title: Taxonomic Categories: Order, Class, Phylum and Kingdom
objectives: Student can define order, class, phylum (division in plants) and kingdom
Student can place an organism such as the housefly, man or mango in the full taxonomic hierarchy
visualIdeas: a pyramid of categories from species at the top to kingdom at the base

topics.title: Five Kingdom Classification
objectives: Student can describe early classifications by Aristotle and the two kingdom system of Linnaeus and why it was inadequate
Student can state Whittaker's five kingdoms and the criteria he used: cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships
visualIdeas: a table comparing the five kingdoms by cell type, cell wall and nutrition

topics.title: Kingdom Monera
objectives: Student can describe bacteria as the sole members of Monera and their wide habitats
Student can classify bacteria by shape: coccus, bacillus, vibrio and spirillum
visualIdeas: the four bacterial shapes side by side

topics.title: Archaebacteria and Eubacteria
objectives: Student can describe archaebacteria (halophiles, thermoacidophiles, methanogens) and their special cell wall
Student can describe eubacteria including cyanobacteria with heterocysts, chemosynthetic and heterotrophic bacteria, and their reproduction
Student can describe mycoplasma as organisms without a cell wall
visualIdeas: a filamentous cyanobacterium with heterocysts
a bacterium dividing by fission

topics.title: Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates and Euglenoids
objectives: Student can state the general features of Protista as single-celled eukaryotes
Student can describe diatoms and their silica walls, dinoflagellates and red tides, and Euglena with its pellicle and two flagella
visualIdeas: a diatom with its two overlapping shells
Euglena with its flagella and eyespot

topics.title: Slime Moulds and Protozoans
objectives: Student can describe slime moulds forming a plasmodium and resistant spores
Student can describe the four groups of protozoans: amoeboid, flagellated, ciliated and sporozoans, with examples
visualIdeas: Paramoecium with cilia beside Amoeba with pseudopodia

topics.title: Kingdom Fungi
objectives: Student can describe the general features of fungi: heterotrophic, hyphae, mycelium and chitin cell walls
Student can describe asexual and sexual reproduction in fungi, including plasmogamy, karyogamy and the dikaryon
visualIdeas: bread mould mycelium with hyphae and sporangia

topics.title: Phycomycetes and Ascomycetes
objectives: Student can describe phycomycetes with aseptate coenocytic mycelium and zygospores, such as Mucor and Rhizopus
Student can describe ascomycetes (sac fungi) with conidia and ascospores, such as yeast and Penicillium
visualIdeas: Mucor with sporangia beside Aspergillus with conidia

topics.title: Basidiomycetes and Deuteromycetes
objectives: Student can describe basidiomycetes such as mushrooms, rusts and smuts, with basidiospores formed on basidia
Student can describe deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi) known only by their asexual stage, such as Alternaria and Trichoderma
visualIdeas: an Agaricus mushroom with gills

topics.title: Kingdom Plantae and Kingdom Animalia
objectives: Student can describe Plantae as eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms, including partly heterotrophic insectivorous and parasitic plants
Student can describe Animalia as heterotrophic multicellular eukaryotes without cell walls that store glycogen or fat and show holozoic nutrition
visualIdeas: a Venus flytrap and Cuscuta beside a typical animal

topics.title: Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
objectives: Student can describe viruses as non-cellular particles with a protein coat and RNA or DNA, and name diseases they cause
Student can describe viroids and prions as infectious agents and lichens as associations of algae and fungi
visualIdeas: a bacteriophage and tobacco mosaic virus structure
a lichen on a tree trunk

topics.title: Systems of Classification
objectives: Student can distinguish artificial, natural and phylogenetic systems of classification
Student can describe numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy
visualIdeas: a timeline from Linnaeus' artificial system to Bentham and Hooker's natural system and phylogenetic systems

topics.title: Algae
objectives: Student can describe algae as chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, mostly aquatic organisms
Student can describe vegetative, asexual and sexual (isogamous, anisogamous, oogamous) reproduction in algae and their economic importance

topics.title: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae

topics.title: Bryophytes
objectives: Student can describe bryophytes as the amphibians of the plant kingdom living in moist shaded places

topics.title: Liverworts and Mosses

the protonema stage of a moss

topics.title: Pteridophytes

objectives: Student can distinguish diploblastic and triploblastic animals

visualIdeas: cross-sections of an acoelomate, a pseudocoelomate and a coelomate
